source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, Subtropical Steppe. Central Spain is the Meseta Central , a plateau of about 600 to 700 metres ringed by mountains, and the ring is what makes its climate. The Cantabrians and the Sistema Central block the moist Atlantic westerlies and the Baetic ranges block Mediterranean air from the south-east, leaving the interior dry. Madrid, at about 667 metres on the southern Meseta, is classed as cold semi-arid, Koppen BSk , which is the subtropical steppe type. The interior is also more continental than the coasts: summers are hot, winters genuinely cold, and the annual temperature range far wider than at any coastal Spanish station. The boundary is not sharp: Madrid's western side grades into a Mediterranean Csa, and the key takes the drier steppe classification for the centre.

question: Which one of the following is not among the principal languages of Jammu and Kashmir?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: D, Monpa. Monpa belongs to Arunachal Pradesh, not to Jammu and Kashmir. It is the language of the Monpa people, about fifty thousand strong, concentrated in Tawang district (where they are the great majority) and in West Kameng, and it is a Tibeto-Burman language written in the Tibetan script. The other three options are all genuinely of Jammu and Kashmir. Koshur is Kashmiri, the single largest language of the territory at close to fifty-three per cent of speakers. Urdu was the official language of the state for decades and remains one of the official languages today. Gujari, or Gojri, is the language of the Gujjar and Bakerwal communities and is spoken by about nine per cent of the population, which places it third after Kashmiri and Dogri. So the odd one out is the one from the eastern Himalaya.

question: The major part of Central Asia is dominated by which one of the following language families?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: D, Altaic. The great majority of Central Asians speak Turkic languages (Kazakh, Uzbek, Kyrgyz and Turkmen among them) and Turkic is the largest of the three families traditionally grouped together as Altaic, alongside Mongolic and Tungusic. The grouping takes its name from the Altai mountains, which sit at roughly the geographical centre of the three, and its speakers spread across Northern, Eastern and Central Asia. On that reckoning Central Asia is Altaic country, and the key follows the classification used in Indian textbooks. One qualification belongs in an honest card: modern linguistics has moved away from treating Altaic as a genuine family. Most linguists now regard it as obsolete as a genetic grouping and attribute the resemblances to long contact (a sprachbund rather than common descent) while a significant academic minority still argues for the family. The name remains the standard label for the region's languages even where the genetic claim is doubted.

question: Which one of the following Articles was defended by Dr. B. R. Ambedkar on the plea that it would be used as ‘a matter of last resort’?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, Article 356. Article 356 lets the President, on a report from the Governor of a State or otherwise, declare that the government of that State cannot be carried on in accordance with the Constitution and assume its functions to himself: what everyone calls President's Rule . When the Constituent Assembly attacked the emergency provisions as a licence for the Centre to strangle the provinces, Ambedkar defended them as an insurance policy, not an instrument of routine government. He set out a ladder for the President to climb before the last rung: first a warning to the State that it is not governing constitutionally, then an order for a fresh election so the electorate can settle the matter, and only if both fail, Central rule. His hope, as the debates record it, was that such articles 'will never be called into operation and that they would remain a dead letter'.

question: What is the ground on which the Supreme Court can refuse relief under Article 32?
opt_a: The aggrieved person can get remedy from another court
opt_b: That disputed facts have to be investigated
opt_c: That no fundamental right has been infringed
opt_d: That the petitioner has not asked for the proper writ applicable to his/her case
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, That no fundamental right has been infringed. Article 32 is not a general grievance window; it is the right to move the Supreme Court 'for the enforcement of the rights conferred by this Part', that is, by Part III. The jurisdiction is therefore keyed to a single question: has a Fundamental Right been violated? If the answer is no, the Court has nothing under Article 32 to enforce, and it refuses relief for want of jurisdiction rather than as a matter of discretion. That makes it the ground in the strict sense. The other three are reasons a Bench may decline in a particular case while the door stays open: a petitioner sent to the High Court under Article 226 may come back, a petitioner who asked for the wrong writ may be granted the right one, and a dispute turning on contested facts may be sent to a forum that can take evidence.

question: The Ministry of Heavy Industries and Public Enterprises consists of
opt_a: the Department of Heavy Industry and the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade
opt_b: the Department of Public Enterprises and the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade
opt_c: the Department of Scientific and Industrial Research and the Department of Heavy Industry
opt_d: the Department of Heavy Industry and the Department of Public Enterprises
source_explanation_raw: Correct: D, the Department of Heavy Industry and the Department of Public Enterprises. The ministry's name at the time of the exam gives the answer: 'Heavy Industries and Public Enterprises' names two halves, and each half was a department. The Department of Heavy Industry handled the engineering, machine-tool, automotive and heavy-electrical sectors and the central public sector undertakings in them. The Department of Public Enterprises was the government's nodal department for policy on central public sector enterprises generally. The Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade, which appears in two of the wrong options, belongs to a different ministry altogether, and the Department of Scientific and Industrial Research belongs to a third.

question: The First Delimitation Commission in India was constituted in
source_explanation_raw: Correct: D, 1952. Delimitation in India is not done by the Election Commission on its own initiative. It is done by a Delimitation Commission set up under a law made by Parliament for that purpose, as Article 82 requires after every census. The first such law was the Delimitation Commission Act, 1952, and the first Commission was constituted under it that year, to redraw parliamentary and assembly constituencies on the basis of the 1951 Census. The earlier dates in the options belong to other founding moments that candidates blur together (the Constituent Assembly's final year, the commencement of the Constitution and the first Census of independent India), none of which produced a Delimitation Commission.

question: Who among the following stated in the Constituent Assembly that on 26th January, 1950, India was going to enter a life of contradictions?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, Dr. B. R. Ambedkar. The line comes from his concluding speech to the Constituent Assembly on 25 November 1949, the day before the Constitution was adopted. Speaking of what would happen when it commenced, he said: 'On the 26th of January 1950, we are going to enter into a life of contradictions. In politics we will have equality and in social and economic life we will have inequality.' The contradiction he named was between the political principle of one person one vote and one vote one value, and a social and economic structure that continued to deny one person one value, and he warned that those who suffered the inequality would eventually blow up the structure of political democracy the Assembly had so laboriously built. The same speech contains his two other famous warnings, against the 'grammar of anarchy' and against hero-worship in politics.

question: The power of the Supreme Court to decide in the case of a dispute between two or more States is called
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, original jurisdiction. A court exercises original jurisdiction when a dispute is brought to it first, not on appeal from a lower court. Article 131 gives the Supreme Court exactly that power over federal disputes, wherever the dispute involves a question on which a legal right depends. It covers disputes between the Government of India and one or more States; between the Government of India and any State or States on one side and one or more other States on the other; and between two or more States. The jurisdiction is exclusive as well as original: no other court in the country can hear a suit of that kind. That is why a boundary or river-water dispute between two States, if framed as a legal right, goes straight to the Supreme Court.

question: Who among the following is the Chairman of the Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister (EAC-PM)?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, Bibek Debroy. The Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister was reconstituted on 25 September 2017 with the economist Bibek Debroy as its Chairman, and he held that office at the time of this February 2020 paper. The other three names in the options were not decoys picked at random: all of them were associated with the same Council, which is what makes the item hard. Ratan P. Watal was its Member-Secretary, and Ashima Goyal and Sajjid Chinoy were among its part-time members. Present-day position, because it has moved twice since the exam: Debroy died on 1 November 2024, Suman Bery of NITI Aayog held additional charge as interim Chairman, and S. Mahendra Dev was appointed Chairman in 2025.

question: Hilsa is the national fish of
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, Bangladesh. Hilsa, called ilish in Bengali, is the national fish of Bangladesh, and the claim is backed by more than sentiment. The fish accounts for about twelve per cent of Bangladesh's total fish production, and Bangladesh supplies roughly ninety-seven per cent of the world's ilish. In August 2017 the country's Department of Patents, Designs and Trademarks recognised it as a Geographical Indication of Bangladesh. Hilsa is anadromous (it lives in the sea and runs up rivers to breed) and the Padma and Meghna runs are the heart of the fishery, which is why the fish is bound up with Bengali food, festivals and even diplomacy.

question: The Vijaynagar Advanced Landing Ground of the Indian Air Force, which was reopened recently, is located in
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, Arunachal Pradesh. Vijaynagar lies in the Changlang district of Arunachal Pradesh, in the far south-east of the State near the Myanmar border, and its airstrip was built in 1962. For more than sixty years it was the settlement's only link with the rest of the country, because no motorable road reached it. The runway had been laid with pierced steel plate, which the humid climate wore out, and heavy aircraft stopped using it in 2016. It was resurfaced in asphalt to about 1,213 metres, and reopened in September 2019: the reopening the paper refers to. An Advanced Landing Ground is precisely this kind of asset: a short forward airstrip near a sensitive frontier, kept usable for transport aircraft and helicopters that supply troops and isolated villages.

question: Rustom-2, which crashed in Karnataka recently, was a/an
source_explanation_raw: Correct: D, unmanned aerial vehicle. Rustom-2, later renamed TAPAS-BH-201, is a twin-engine medium-altitude long-endurance unmanned aerial vehicle built by the Aeronautical Development Establishment of the Defence Research and Development Organisation, developed from the earlier Rustom-H. It is a surveillance platform, not a strike aircraft: DRDO has stated plainly that it is a UAV and not an unmanned combat aerial vehicle. The crash the paper refers to happened on 17 September 2019 near Jodichikkenahalli in Chitradurga district of Karnataka, during a trial from the Aeronautical Test Range at Challakere; nobody was hurt, which is one of the practical arguments for unmanned testing in the first place. The programme recovered from it: satellite communication was demonstrated in 2020, an altitude of 28,000 feet with eighteen hours of endurance by March 2022, and the two-hundredth flight by June 2023.

question: The maiden trilateral naval exercise involving India, Singapore and Thailand was held at
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, Port Blair. The maiden Singapore-India-Thailand Maritime Exercise, SITMEX, ran from 16 to 20 September 2019 and was hosted by India. It was built in two parts: a harbour phase at Port Blair in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, with expert exchanges, pre-sail conferences and even basketball between the ships' teams, followed by a sea phase in the Andaman Sea. India contributed the guided-missile destroyer INS Ranvir, the missile corvette INS Kora and the offshore patrol vessel INS Sukanya, along with maritime patrol aircraft; Singapore sent the frigate RSS Tenacious and Thailand the frigate HTMS Kraburi. Port Blair is the natural venue because the Andaman and Nicobar Command sits astride the approaches to the Strait of Malacca, which is exactly the water the three navies were exercising to keep open.

question: The creation of a Federal Court in India was advocated by which of the following Acts/Commissions?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, The Government of India Act, 1935. The 1935 Act was the first to provide for a Federal Court, and it did so because it was the first to attempt a federation. A federal structure needs an umpire to settle disputes between the Centre and the units and to interpret the constitutional division of powers, and Part IX of the Act created one for that purpose. The Court was constituted in 1937 with an original jurisdiction over disputes between the federation and the provinces, an appellate jurisdiction in cases involving interpretation of the Act, and an advisory jurisdiction on references by the Governor-General. It functioned until the Supreme Court of India replaced it in 1950, and it is the direct ancestor of the jurisdictions listed in Articles 131, 132 and 143 today.

question: Who founded the ‘Seva Samiti’ at Allahabad in 1914?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, Hridayanath Kunzru. Kunzru was a member of the Servants of India Society, the body Gopal Krishna Gokhale had founded in 1905 to train men for the full-time, salaried, non-political service of the country, and he became its life President in 1936. The Seva Samiti he set up at Allahabad in 1914 belongs to that tradition: a voluntary social-service organisation for relief work, work at fairs and pilgrimages, and civic service, rather than a political association. Kunzru's later public life ran along the same line: he was among the founders of Indian Scouting and became the first National Commissioner of the Bharat Scouts and Guides, serving from 1952 to 1957.

question: The State of Hyderabad in the Deccan officially acceded to the Indian Union in the year
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, 1950. The word carrying the weight in the stem is 'officially'. Three separate dates belong to Hyderabad's absorption, and only the last is an accession in the legal sense. In September 1948 the Indian Army entered the State in the operation code-named Polo, and the Nizam's forces surrendered at five in the evening on 17 September: a military settlement, not an instrument of accession. On 24 November 1949 the Nizam issued a firman accepting that the Constitution of India would apply to Hyderabad. The Instrument of Accession itself was signed on 25 January 1950, the day before the Constitution came into force, and the Nizam took the new title of Rajpramukh of Hyderabad as a Part B State of the Union. That signature in 1950 is what the key is pointing at.

question: The Hunter Commission (1882) appointed to survey the state of education in India
opt_c: endorsed the Despatch of 1854 with greater emphasis on primary education
opt_d: criticized the grants-in-aid system of schooling
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, endorsed the Despatch of 1854 with greater emphasis on primary education. The Commission of 1882, presided over by William Wilson Hunter , was appointed to review how far the education policy laid down in Wood's Despatch of 1854 had actually been carried out. Its conclusion was continuity with a shift of weight. The framework of the Despatch stood, but the state's first duty was declared to be the extension and improvement of elementary education for the mass of the people, which was to be handed to the newly created district and municipal boards. Secondary and collegiate education was to pass progressively to private hands supported by grants-in-aid. So the Despatch was reaffirmed, not overturned, and primary schooling was pushed to the front of the queue.

question: The power to legislate on all matters relating to elections to Panchayats lies with
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, the State Legislatures. Article 243K settles this in four clauses. The first vests the superintendence, direction and control of the preparation of electoral rolls and the conduct of Panchayat elections in a State Election Commission, headed by a State Election Commissioner appointed by the Governor. The fourth is the one the question asks about: subject to the provisions of the Constitution, the Legislature of a State may by law make provision with respect to all matters relating to, or in connection with, elections to the Panchayats. So conducting the elections and legislating about them are two different functions given to two different authorities, and the law-making half belongs to the State Legislature.

question: The 11th Schedule of the Constitution of India distributes powers between
opt_a: the Union and the State Legislatures
opt_b: the State Legislatures and the Panchayat
opt_c: the Municipal Corporation and the Panchayat
opt_d: the Gram Sabha and the Panchayat
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, the State Legislatures and the Panchayat. The Eleventh Schedule was inserted by the 73rd Amendment and is read with Article 243G, which says that the Legislature of a State may by law endow the Panchayats with such powers and authority as may be necessary to enable them to function as institutions of self-government, including with respect to the preparation of plans and the implementation of schemes for the twenty-nine matters listed in that Schedule. The Schedule is therefore a menu, and the State Legislature is the hand that serves from it: agriculture, minor irrigation, animal husbandry, rural housing, drinking water, roads, poverty alleviation, primary education, health, the public distribution system and the rest. Devolution is not automatic, which is precisely why the two parties in the answer are the State Legislature on one side and the Panchayat on the other.

question: The provisions of the Constitution of India pertaining to the institution of Panchayat do not apply to which one of the following States?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, Meghalaya. Article 243M is the exemption clause of Part IX, and it names three States outright: Nagaland, Meghalaya and Mizoram. The reason is that a different and older system of local self-government is already in place there. In Meghalaya it is the Autonomous District Councils of the Sixth Schedule (the Khasi Hills, Jaintia Hills and Garo Hills councils), which perform the functions a Panchayat would otherwise perform. Article 243M also exempts certain areas elsewhere, such as the Scheduled Areas and the hill areas of Manipur, but Meghalaya is the only option here kept out of Part IX as a whole.

question: Which one of the following rivers does not drain into Black Sea?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, Volga. The Volga is Europe's longest river, about 3,530 kilometres from the Valdai Hills to a delta below Astrakhan, and that delta opens into the Caspian Sea, not the Black Sea. Because the Caspian has no outlet to any ocean, the Volga belongs to an inland drainage basin: it is the largest river in the world that ends in a closed sea. The other three all reach the Black Sea. The Danube crosses or touches ten countries and enters through a delta on the Romanian and Ukrainian border; the Dnieper runs down through Belarus and Ukraine past Kyiv; and the Don flows into the Sea of Azov, which connects to the Black Sea through the Strait of Kerch, so it drains into the Black Sea system.

question: The National Water Academy (NWA) is located at
source_explanation_raw: Correct: D, Khadakwasla. The National Water Academy is the in-house training institute of the Central Water Commission, and it sits at Khadakwasla near Pune, on the campus of the Central Water and Power Research Station. It runs induction training for newly recruited officers of the Central Water Engineering Service, orientation and refresher courses, and capacity-building programmes on dam safety, flood forecasting, hydrology and water management for engineers from the Centre, the States and neighbouring countries. Khadakwasla itself, about sixteen kilometres south-west of Pune, is a cluster of national institutions built around the reservoir: besides the water research station it holds the National Defence Academy and the Defence Institute of Advanced Technology.

question: Which one of the following is the correct sequence of formation of the Commissions starting from the earliest?
opt_a: Finance Commission, Planning Commission, Investment Commission, Election Commission
opt_b: Election Commission, Planning Commission, Finance Commission, Investment Commission
opt_c: Planning Commission, Election Commission, Finance Commission, Investment Commission
opt_d: Investment Commission, Finance Commission, Planning Commission, Election Commission
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, Election Commission, Planning Commission, Finance Commission, Investment Commission. Three sourced dates settle the whole item. The Election Commission of India came into being on 25 January 1950 under Article 324, the day before the Constitution commenced, which is why that date is now observed as National Voters' Day. The Planning Commission followed within weeks, created by a government resolution on 15 March 1950 with no constitutional or statutory basis at all. The First Finance Commission was constituted in 1951 under Article 280, with K. C. Neogy as Chairman, and reported for the period 1952 to 1957. The Investment Commission is a creature of the 2000s and comes last. Only option (b) puts those first three in the order 25 January 1950, 15 March 1950, 1951.

question: The formulation of policy in respect to Intellectual Property Rights (IPRs) is the responsibility of
opt_a: the Ministry of Law and Justice
opt_b: the Department of Science and Technology
opt_c: the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade
opt_d: the Ministry of Human Resource Development
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade. Intellectual property in India is administered as an industrial-policy subject rather than a legal or scientific one, and the department that owns it is the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade in the Ministry of Commerce and Industry. It houses the Office of the Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks, under which the patent offices, the trade marks registry, the designs office and the geographical indications registry work, and it is the nodal body that framed the National Intellectual Property Rights Policy of 2016. That policy is also where India's position on the World Trade Organization's TRIPS Agreement and the Doha Development Agenda is set out.

question: Which one of the following is the latest addition to the AYUSH group of health care system?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, Sowa-Rigpa. The acronym AYUSH was built from Ayurveda, Yoga and Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha and Homoeopathy, and those were the systems the department, later the Ministry, began with. Sowa-Rigpa is the addition. It is the Himalayan and Tibetan system of medicine practised in Ladakh, Himachal Pradesh, Sikkim and Arunachal Pradesh, and the Government of India recognised it in 2010 as a science of healing, later approving a National Institute of Sowa-Rigpa at Leh in Ladakh for research and development in it. Unani and Siddha are in the acronym itself and so cannot be the latest addition, and Reiki is not part of AYUSH at all.

question: Which one of the following is the nodal agency in India for the United Nations Environment Programme?
opt_a: The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
opt_b: The Ministry of Science and Technology
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change. The Ministry describes itself as the nodal agency in the country for the United Nations Environment Programme, and in the same breath for the South Asia Co-operative Environment Programme, the International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development and the follow-up of the United Nations Conference on Environment and Development. The work is done through its International Cooperation Division, which is also the nodal division for the Global Environment Facility. That fits the Ministry's general character: it is the nodal agency in the Central Government for planning, promoting, coordinating and overseeing India's environmental and forestry policies and programmes, so international environmental cooperation naturally sits with it.

question: According to the Census 2011, in India, what is the percentage of people (approximately) considered to be migrants (internal), i.e., now settled in a place different from their previous residence?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, 35%. Census 2011 counted 453.6 million migrants in a population of 1,210,854,977, which works out to about 37.8 per cent. Of the four figures offered, 35 per cent is by far the closest, which is what the word 'approximately' in the stem is doing. The scale surprises people because migration is counted by place of last residence , so it includes every short move: a woman who marries into the next village, a family that shifts from one town to another within the same district. Those short-distance moves, not the long-distance labour migration that dominates the news, are the bulk of the number. Marriage is the single largest reason recorded, which is also why the female migration rate runs far above the male one.

question: Suppose an agricultural labourer earns ₹400 per day in her village. She gets a job to work as babysitter in a nearby town @ ₹700 per day. She chose to work as agricultural labourer. Which one of the following is the opportunity cost of the agricultural labourer?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, ₹700. Opportunity cost is the value of the next best alternative given up when a choice is made, and it is measured by what you did not take, never by what you took. By working in her village for ₹400 a day she gave up the babysitting job in town that would have paid ₹700 a day. So the opportunity cost of her choice is ₹700: the whole value of the alternative forgone , not the difference between the two. The ₹300 gap is the net loss of income from her decision, which is a different quantity and the trap the option set is built around.

question: Match List—I with List—II and select the correct answer using the code given below the Lists: List—I (Market structure) A. Perfect competition B. Monopoly C. Monopolistic competition D. Oligopoly List—II (Characteristic) 1. Only one producer selling one commodity 2. Few producers selling similar or almost similar products 3. Many producers selling differentiated products 4. Many producers selling similar products Code:
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, A B C D : 4 1 3 2. Two variables define these four market structures: how many sellers there are, and whether their product is identical or differentiated. Perfect competition has many producers selling an identical product, which is entry 4, many producers selling similar products. Monopoly is the single seller, entry 1, only one producer selling one commodity. Monopolistic competition keeps the large number of sellers but gives each a product of its own through branding, packaging or quality, which is entry 3, many producers selling differentiated products. Oligopoly is the small-numbers case, entry 2, few producers selling similar or almost similar products. So A is 4, B is 1, C is 3 and D is 2.

question: Which one of the following was the host country for World Tourism Day, 2019?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, India. World Tourism Day is observed on 27 September under the auspices of the United Nations World Tourism Organization, and a different member country hosts the official celebration each year. India was the host for 2019, and the theme that year was 'Tourism and jobs: a better future for all': a theme chosen to press the point that tourism is among the largest generators of employment, especially for women and young people, which is precisely why India wanted it. The neighbouring years are worth carrying alongside: Qatar in 2017 on sustainable tourism, Hungary in 2018 on digital transformation, the Mercosur bloc in 2020 on rural development, and Ivory Coast in 2021 on inclusive growth.

question: BRICS Summit, 2020 will be hosted by
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, Russia. The chairship of BRICS rotates among the members, and 2020 was Russia's turn. The 12th BRICS Summit was chaired by Vladimir Putin and had been planned for Saint Petersburg on 21 to 23 July 2020; the pandemic forced it online, and it was finally held by video conference on 17 November 2020. Read the rotation on either side of it and the pattern is clear: Brazil hosted the 11th summit at Brasilia on 13 and 14 November 2019, and India chaired the 13th on 9 September 2021, also by video conference. The paper was set in February 2020, which is why it asks in the future tense about a summit that had not yet happened.

question: The Government of India has recently constituted a civilian award in the name of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel in the field of contribution to
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, unity and integrity of India. The award instituted in 2019 in Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel's name is the Sardar Patel National Unity Award, and it is the highest civilian honour in the field of contribution to the unity and integrity of India. It is announced on 31 October, Patel's birth anniversary, which is observed as Rashtriya Ekta Diwas or National Unity Day: the same date on which the Run for Unity is held. The choice of field is the point of the naming: Patel is remembered above all for bringing the princely States into the Union, so an award in his name for national unity is the obvious fit, and the other three fields already have their own honours.
